content.text:
Start working on Linear ticket eng-1832 by fetching its details and creating a dedicated git worktree.

## Steps

### 1. Validate input
- `eng-1832` should be a Linear ticket ID like `ENG-1271`. If missing or malformed, ask the user.

### 2. Fetch ticket details from Linear
- Use `mcp__linear-server__get_issue` with the issue ID `eng-1832`
- Extract: title, description, and `branchName` (Linear provides this)
- If the Linear tool is unavailable, ask the user for a branch name manually

### 3. Determine branch name
- Use the `branchName` field from Linear if available (it's already formatted correctly)
- Otherwise derive it: lowercase the ticket ID + hyphenated slug of the title
  - Example: `ENG-1271 Implement filter search` → `eng-1271-implement-filter-search`
  - Strip special characters, replace spaces with hyphens, truncate to ~60 chars

### 4. Create git worktree
Run these from the repo root (the main working directory, not an existing worktree):

```bash
# Fetch latest main so the worktree starts from up-to-date origin/main
git fetch origin main

# Check if branch already exists
git branch --list <branch-name>

# Check if worktree already exists
git worktree list | grep <branch-name>
```

- **If worktree already exists**: skip to step 5, just `cd` into `.claude/worktrees/<branch-name>`
- **If branch does NOT exist**: `git worktree add -b <branch-name> .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> origin/main`
- **If branch already exists but no worktree**: reset the branch to `origin/main` first, then add the worktree:
  ```bash
  git branch -f <branch-name> origin/main
  git worktree add .claude/worktrees/<branch-name> <branch-name>
  ```

### 5. Enter the worktree
**Do NOT use the `EnterWorktree` tool** — it always creates a brand-new worktree and will duplicate the one you just created.

Instead, use `cd` to switch into the worktree directory:
```bash
cd .claude/worktrees/<branch-name>
```

All subsequent commands should run from this path.

### 6. Install dependencies and set up the worktree
After entering the worktree, run the following to bootstrap the environment:

```bash
pnpm install
```

This is required because worktrees share git objects but each needs its own `node_modules`.

### 6b. Copy .env files from the main repo into the worktree
`.env` files are gitignored, so each worktree needs its own copies. After `pnpm install`, copy all `.env` files (excluding `.env.example` files) from the main repo root into the matching relative paths in the worktree.

The main repo root is the working directory you were in before entering the worktree (e.g. `/Users/trang.doan/Desktop/code/discourse-graph`).

Run:
```bash
# From the main repo root, find all .env files (not .env.example) and copy them into the worktree
find . -name ".env*" \
  -not -name ".env.example" \
  -not -path "./.git/*" \
  -not -path "./node_modules/*" \
  -not -path "./.claude/worktrees/*" \
  | while read f; do
      dest=".claude/worktrees/<branch-name>/$f"
      mkdir -p "$(dirname "$dest")"
      cp "$f" "$dest"
    done
```

Report which files were copied so the user can confirm.

### 7. Ask the user which app to start
Ask the user which app they want to run in dev mode. Common options:
- **Roam**: `turbo dev --F=roam`
- **Obsidian**: `export SUPABASE_USE_DB=local && turbo dev`
- **None**: just set up the environment without starting a dev server

If the user says Roam, also switch the Roam dev symlink:
```bash
ln -sfn $(pwd)/apps/roam/dist ~/roam-ext-dev
```
and remind them to reload the developer extension in Roam.

Run the chosen dev command in the background so the user can continue working.

### 8. Ingest any saved session context
The branch may have been worked on before (e.g. reset from an existing branch).
Check for recorded session context:

```bash
bash ~/.claude/scripts/session-context.sh resolve
```

- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=yes`, **read the `CONTEXT_FILE`** and load it as working context
  (`Next step`, `Open questions`, `Key decisions`, `Dead ends`).
- If `CONTEXT_EXISTS=no` or the command errors, continue — this is a fresh start.

### 9. Show context
After setup, display:
- Ticket ID and title
- Branch name you're on
- Brief description from the ticket (if available)
- Which app dev server is running (if any)
- If prior session context was found: its `TL;DR` and `Next step`
- A short "ready to work" confirmation
- Remind the user they can run `/checkpoint` to save session context before wrapping up

# eslint-plugin-obsidianmd

## Installation

You'll first need to install [ESLint](https://eslint.org/):

```sh
npm i eslint --save-dev
```

Next, install `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd`:

```sh
npm install eslint-plugin-obsidianmd --save-dev
```

## Usage

With the release of ESLint v9, the default configuration file is now `eslint.config.js`.

### Flat Config (`eslint.config.js`) - Recommended for ESLint v9+

To use the recommended configuration, add it to your `eslint.config.js` file. This will enable all the recommended rules.

```javascript
// eslint.config.mjs
import tsparser from "@typescript-eslint/parser";
import { defineConfig } from "eslint/config";
import obsidianmd from "eslint-plugin-obsidianmd";

export default defineConfig([
  ...obsidianmd.configs.recommended,
  {
    files: ["**/*.ts"],
    languageOptions: {
      parser: tsparser,
      parserOptions: { project: "./tsconfig.json" },
    },

    // You can add your own configuration to override or add rules
    rules: {
      // example: turn off a rule from the recommended set
      "obsidianmd/sample-names": "off",
      // example: add a rule not in the recommended set and set its severity
      "obsidianmd/prefer-file-manager-trash": "error",
    },
  },
]);

```

### Legacy Config (`.eslintrc`)

<details>
<summary>Click here for ESLint v8 and older</summary>

To use the recommended configuration, extend it in your `.eslintrc` file:

```json
{
  "extends": ["plugin:obsidianmd/recommended"]
}
```

You can also override or add rules:

```json
{
  "extends": ["plugin:obsidianmd/recommended"],
  "rules": {
    "obsidianmd/sample-names": "off",
    "obsidianmd/prefer-file-manager-trash": "error"
  }
}
```

</details>

=== obsidian AGENTS.md ===
You are working on the Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Obsidian Style Guide

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content
- Use Obsidian DOM helpers instead: `createEl()`, `createDiv()`, `createSpan()`

### App instance

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

### Event listeners

- Register all event listeners via `this.registerEvent()` so they are automatically cleaned up on plugin unload

### UI text

- Use sentence case in settings headings and labels (not title case)
- Prefer `setHeading()` over raw HTML heading elements (`<h1>`, `<h2>`, etc.)

### Commands

- Do not set default hotkeys — they conflict with other plugins
- Use the correct callback type: `callback` for always-available commands, `checkCallback` when the command is conditionally available, or the editor variants for editor-scoped commands

content.text:
Cleaned up. Here's what I found and the plan.

## Findings from a real trial run

I installed `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd@0.4.1` in the worktree and ran it against `apps/obsidian` to get real numbers rather than guess.

**Compatibility is now fine** — this is what the old PR was blocked on:

| Peer | Required | Repo has |
|---|---|---|
| `eslint` | `>=9.19.0` | `9.39.5` ✅ |
| `typescript-eslint` | `^8.35.1` | `8.67.0` ✅ |
| `obsidian` | `1.8.7` | resolves to `1.8.7` ✅ |
| `@eslint/js` | `^9.30.1` | `9.29.0` ⚠️ minor bump |

No catalog gymnastics needed. The old PR's `catalog:obsidian` ESLint-9 scoping is entirely obsolete.

**Three integration problems the plain `...obsidianmd.configs.recommended` append hits:**

1. **Hard crash.** The recommended set registers `manifest.json`/`package.json` via `@eslint/json`, and our shared React rules then run against them: `TypeError: sourceCode.getAllComments is not a function`. Fix is to scope the `@repo/eslint-config` blocks to script files.
2. **14 phantom `'React' is not defined`.** obsidianmd's config comes after ours and resets `languageOptions.globals` + re-enables core `no-undef` for TS. Needs ordering/override handling.
3. **Bundled noise.** The plugin depends on `eslint-plugin-security`, `-import`, `-depend`, `@microsoft/eslint-plugin-sdl`, `@eslint-community/eslint-comments`. Those contribute **43 findings that have nothing to do with Obsidian review** (26 `eslint-comments/require-description`, 13 `disable-enable-pair`, 2 `depend/ban-dependencies` complaining about `dotenv`), plus 8 new "unused eslint-disable directive" fatals.

**Violation counts** (baseline today is already 112 — `pnpm lint` is not clean, CI tolerates it because reviewdog only fails on *added* lines):

| | count |
|---|---|
| Baseline (current config) | 112 |
| With obsidianmd recommended | 280 |
| — actual `obsidianmd/*` rules | **99** |
| — bundled non-Obsidian plugins | 43 + 8 fatals |

The 99 Obsidian findings break down as **46 auto-fixable** (`prefer-window-timers` 27, `prefer-create-el` 15, `prefer-instanceof` 4) and **53 manual** — `rule-custom-message[no-console]` 22 (matches your existing no-console rule for Obsidian), `no-static-styles-assignment` 15, `ui/sentence-case` 10, plus a handful of command-naming and `Vault.delete()` hits.

## Proposed plan

**1. Dependency** — add `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd@^0.4.1` to `apps/obsidian` devDeps, bump `@eslint/js` to `^9.30.1` in `packages/eslint-config`. (Already installed in the worktree from the trial — that's the current diff.)

**2. Config wiring** in `apps/obsidian/eslint.config.mjs` — scope shared blocks to script files so JSON linting works, order obsidianmd so it doesn't clobber globals, restore `no-undef: off` for TS, and turn off the bundled non-Obsidian plugins that aren't part of store review. Keeps the change local to the Obsidian app; `packages/eslint-config` gets only the `@eslint/js` bump.

**3. Auto-fix pass** — `eslint . --fix` for the 46 mechanical ones, reviewed as its own commit so it's easy to skim.

**4. Manual fixes** — scoped by category; the 22 `no-console` hits should mostly become `new Notice()` per the existing Obsidian rule.

**5. Agent side** (the ticket's second half) — wire `pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint` into `apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md` as a required post-change step, and cross-reference the existing `obsidian-plugin-guidelines` skill. Note that skill lives at `.claude/skills/` which is **gitignored** (`.gitignore:43`) — so it isn't shared with the team. Moving it to the tracked `skills/` directory is worth doing here.

**6. Verification** — `pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint` (expect obsidianmd count at 0), `check-types`, `build`, and load the built plugin in the vault to confirm the autofixes didn't break runtime behavior.

One scoping call to make:

content.text:
One correction on the second answer: those bundled plugins **do** fire inside `apps/obsidian` — they're transitive deps of `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` and its `recommended` config activates them there. They produce 43 findings + 8 new "unused eslint-disable directive" errors in the Obsidian app itself. They don't leak into roam/website (config is per-workspace), so if that was the concern, you're covered. Since you chose config-only, I'll leave them enabled and they'll surface as warnings alongside everything else.

## Final plan — ENG-1832

**Scope: wire up the linter. No code fixes.** All 99 obsidianmd findings (plus the 43 bundled ones) land as visible warnings in the IDE and on changed lines in CI. No source files in `src/` are touched.

**1. Dependencies**
- `apps/obsidian/package.json`: add `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd@^0.4.1` (already installed in the worktree from the trial — this is the current diff)
- `packages/eslint-config/package.json`: bump `@eslint/js` `^9.29.0` → `^9.30.1` to satisfy the peer

**2. `apps/obsidian/eslint.config.mjs`** — the only real work. Four things, each fixing a concrete failure I hit:
- Scope `@repo/eslint-config` blocks to `**/*.{js,mjs,cjs,jsx,ts,tsx,mts,cts}` so React rules stop crashing on the JSON files obsidianmd registers
- Append `obsidianmd.configs.recommended`
- Re-assert `no-undef: "off"` and our globals for TS after it, killing the 14 phantom `'React' is not defined`
- Comment explaining *why* the scoping exists, so nobody "simplifies" it back into a crash

**3. `apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md`** — document that `pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint` is a required step after Obsidian changes, and that `--fix` handles the mechanical rules. This is the ticket's "agents can automatically modify its code to fit this lint" half.

**4. Move `obsidian-plugin-guidelines` skill from `.claude/skills/` → `skills/`** so it's actually tracked and shared. Right now `.gitignore:43` (`.claude/*`) means only you have it. Say the word if you'd rather split this into its own ticket.

**5. Verification**
- `pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint` — runs clean (no crash), reports the expected ~280 warnings, exit code < 2
- `pnpm --dir apps/obsidian check-types` and `build` — unchanged from baseline
- Confirm `pnpm --dir apps/roam lint` and website lint are byte-identical to before, proving no leakage
- Open a file with a known violation in the IDE and confirm the squiggle appears — that's the ticket's literal "Done When"

**Follow-up ticket** to file: fix the 99 violations (46 auto-fixable, 53 manual — 22 of which are `no-console`, already against your Obsidian house rule).

content.text:
That reframes the whole ticket. Here's the revised plan.

## The key discovery

`eslint-plugin-only-warn` in `packages/eslint-config/base.js` monkey-patches ESLint globally at import time and forces **every** rule to warn. I confirmed explicit `"error"` severity does not defeat it. So as long as a config imports `@repo/eslint-config`, the error/warn distinction you care about is destroyed — every obsidianmd store-blocker arrives as an indistinguishable warning in a pile of 280.

So the store gate has to be a config that never imports the shared base. I built and ran one:

```
ERRORS total 37
  22 obsidianmd/rule-custom-message
  15 obsidianmd/no-static-styles-assignment
WARNINGS total 0
```

Zero noise. And the file breakdown matters more:

| File | Rule | Count |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/build.ts`, `compile.ts`, `generate-test-data.ts`, `setup-test-data.ts` | `rule-custom-message` (no-console) | **22** |
| `src/components/canvas/DiscourseToolPanel.tsx` | `no-static-styles-assignment` | 11 |
| `src/components/ModifyNodeModal.tsx` | `no-static-styles-assignment` | 2 |
| `src/components/canvas/utils/relationUtils.tsx` | `no-static-styles-assignment` | 2 |

**All 22 console hits are in `scripts/`** — build tooling that never ships to the store. Exclude `scripts/**` and your real store-blocking surface is **15 inline-style assignments across 3 files.**

The genuinely dangerous error-level rules — `detach-leaves`, `no-sample-code`, `sample-names`, `platform`, `regex-lookbehind`, `no-plugin-as-component`, `no-view-references-in-plugin`, `no-unsupported-api`, `no-forbidden-elements`, `settings-tab/*` — all report **0**. You're already clean on everything that has historically gotten plugins pulled.

Given that, "config only, no code fixes" no longer makes sense to me — 15 fixes in 3 files is smaller than the config work itself, and fixing them is what lets the gate actually block CI instead of being one more ignorable warning stream. I'd flip that call unless you disagree.

## Plan

**1. `packages/eslint-config/obsidian-store.js`** *(new — prototype already working in the worktree)*
Standalone export that pulls obsidianmd's recommended set, keeps only its **error-level** `obsidianmd/*` rules, and drops everything else. Lives here rather than in `apps/obsidian` because this package already depends on `prefer-arrow-functions`, `react-hooks`, and `turbo` — those namespaces must be registered or existing `eslint-disable` comments in your source raise `Definition for rule ... was not found`. Add `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` and export `./obsidian-store`.

**2. `apps/obsidian/eslint.config.store.mjs`** *(new)* — thin wrapper adding `parserOptions` and ignoring `scripts/**`, `dist/**`.

**3. `apps/obsidian/package.json`** — `"lint:store": "eslint . --config eslint.config.store.mjs --no-config-lookup"`. Separate process is required; sharing one with the main config re-triggers the only-warn patch.

**4. Fix the 15 inline styles** — `element.style.x = …` → CSS classes in `styles.css`. `DiscourseToolPanel.tsx` carries 11 of them.

**5. Leave `eslint.config.mjs` alone.** Your day-to-day lint keeps its current 112-warning baseline and reviewdog behavior — this PR doesn't touch it, so no risk to roam/website. The obsidianmd *warn*-level rules (`prefer-window-timers`, `prefer-create-el`, `ui/sentence-case`, etc., 62 findings) are deliberately **not** wired in; per your call, style advice isn't what this ticket is for. Worth a follow-up ticket since 46 are auto-fixable, but not here.

**6. CI** — add `lint:store` as a job that fails the build. This is the actual "systemic way" the ticket asks for: it can go red, unlike a warning.

**7. `apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md`** — document `pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint:store` as the pre-PR gate, and that a failure means store rejection risk.

**8. Verification** — `lint:store` exits 0 after the fixes; `check-types` and `build` unchanged; roam/website lint byte-identical; load the built plugin in the vault to confirm the CSS-class migration didn't visually regress the tool panel.

Two things to confirm:

Done. ENG-1832 is implemented and verified.

## What landed

**The gate** — [packages/eslint-config/obsidian-store.js](packages/eslint-config/obsidian-store.js) (new) + [apps/obsidian/eslint.config.store.mjs](apps/obsidian/eslint.config.store.mjs) (new), run via `pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint:store`. It carries **only obsidianmd's error-level rules** — the store blockers — and reports nothing else. Hosted in `packages/eslint-config` because it needs the `preferArrows`/`react-hooks`/`turbo` namespaces registered, otherwise your existing `eslint-disable` comments raise `Definition for rule ... was not found`.

It runs as its own process and never imports `@repo/eslint-config`. That's load-bearing: `eslint-plugin-only-warn` patches ESLint globally on import and forces everything to warn, which is exactly the distinction you said matters.

**The 15 fixes** — Tailwind wherever the values were static:
- [DiscourseToolPanel.tsx](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/DiscourseToolPanel.tsx:22) — drag ghost's 11 assignments became two class constants; only `transform` stays dynamic, now via Obsidian's `setCssProps`
- [ModifyNodeModal.tsx:170](apps/obsidian/src/components/ModifyNodeModal.tsx:170) — `position = "fixed"` was dead code, the element's className already had `fixed`; the textarea auto-resize moved to `setCssProps`
- [relationUtils.tsx:1466](apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/utils/relationUtils.tsx:1466) — Safari repaint hack now toggles Tailwind's `hidden`

No `styles.css` changes were needed — Tailwind covered all of it.

**CI** — blocking `obsidian-store-compliance` job. **Docs** — [apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md](apps/obsidian/AGENTS.md) explains the command, why it's separate from `pnpm lint`, and that failures must be fixed rather than suppressed.

`scripts/` is exempt, per your call — that removed all 22 `no-console` errors as store-irrelevant.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `lint:store` | exit 0 |
| Negative test (added `el.style.color`) | caught as **error**, exit 1 |
| `check-types` | exit 0 |
| Main `pnpm lint` | 112 → 112, unchanged |
| Roam lint | 538 messages, 0 errors, no obsidianmd leakage |
| `build` | 0 errors |
| Tailwind CSS emission | `.h-\[50px\]`, `.w-\[50px\]`, `.hidden`, `.fixed`, `pointer-events-none`, `items-center`, `left-0`, `top-0` all present in `dist/styles.css` |
| Built bundle + vault mirror | both contain the new class string |

**One thing I did not verify: the drag-ghost interaction itself.** The build is mirrored to your testVault, but I haven't dragged a node type onto the canvas to confirm the ghost still tracks the cursor and hides correctly inside the panel. That's the only behavioral risk in the diff. Want me to drive Obsidian over CDP and check it?

Two notes for the PR: `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` wants `@eslint/js@^9.30.1` and `packages/eslint-config` pins `^9.29.0` — install succeeded, so it's a cosmetic peer bump you may want anyway. And the 62 warn-level obsidianmd findings (46 auto-fixable) are deliberately not wired in — worth a follow-up ticket.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/trang.doan/.claude/skills/create-pr

# Create PR

Get the branch reviewer-ready, then open the PR. Work the three phases in order —
the self-review changes the diff, and the diff is what the body describes.

`ARGUMENTS` may name a base branch. Otherwise infer it: if this branch was built on
another open PR's branch, target that branch and say so in the body; else `main`.

## Phase 1 — Trim the comments

Only comments **you added on this branch**. Never rewrite comments that belong to
committed work — it inflates the diff with churn a reviewer has to read past.

```bash
git diff --stat "$BASE"...HEAD
git diff "$BASE"...HEAD | grep -nE '^\+\s*(//|/\*|\*|\{/\*)'
```

**Every surviving comment is one line.** Multi-line blocks and JSDoc paragraphs get
compressed, not preserved.

**Keep** a comment only when it says something the code cannot:

- A platform or build quirk with a non-obvious cause — a host CSS rule that outranks
  a utility class, a missing preflight, a library default that bites.
- A deliberate choice a reader would otherwise "fix": an uncontrolled input, a
  suppressed default, a two-step interaction, a guard that looks redundant.
- Why an obvious simpler approach does *not* work.
- A layout or structural decision that is easy to tidy up and thereby break.
- A cross-file invariant that is invisible from this file alone.

**Delete** a comment when it:

- Restates the line below it, or narrates what a well-named function already says.
- Defends a choice nobody would reverse (the ordinary, expected implementation).
- Documents code that no longer exists after a rewrite.
- Is a section banner or a decorative divider.

Ambiguity test: *if I deleted this, would a competent reviewer make a wrong change?*
No → delete it.

## Phase 2 — Self-review the diff

Read the repo's own rules first and check the diff against them, because these are
exactly the comments a reviewer or bot will leave:

```bash
cat AGENTS.md CLAUDE.md STYLE_GUIDE.md 2>/dev/null
find . -name AGENTS.md -not -path '*/node_modules/*'   # per-app rules override the root
```

Fix anything the diff violates. Common catches:

- Inline `style={{...}}` for a static value where a utility class works. Computed
  values (per-item colours) legitimately stay inline.
- Hand-rolled CSS where the platform exposes a variable or an existing class.
- `type` vs `interface`; missing explicit return types; `any`.
- Function declarations where the codebase uses arrow functions.
- Positional-index assumptions across two lists that can differ.
- Console logging in apps that require a user-facing notice instead.
- New dependencies where the platform already ships an equivalent.

Then the checks the CI will run, and the project's own verification story:

```bash
pnpm check-types && pnpm lint      # in the changed app
npx prettier --check <changed files>
```

If the change is observable at runtime, exercise it and say so in the body with
concrete numbers. A body that claims "verified" without saying how is worth less
than one that names what was measured.

## Phase 3 — Write the body and open it

Lead with what the reviewer needs to decide, not with a narration of the diff — they
can read the diff. Keep it scannable; drop any section that would be empty.

```markdown
<One or two sentences: the problem, and the shape of the fix.>

## Review focus

- `path/to/file.ts` — <what to look at here and why it matters>
- <the riskiest change, named explicitly>

## Decisions worth challenging

- **<Decision>** — <why this way, and the alternative rejected.>
- <Any deviation from the ticket or from a sibling implementation, and why.>

## Verification

- <checks run>
- <runtime evidence, with numbers>
- <what is deliberately not covered, e.g. no unit tests and why>

## Known limits

<Edge cases documented rather than fixed, and why that is the right call. Omit if none.>
```

Rules for the body:

- Name files by path so the reviewer can jump straight to them.
- Surface deviations from the ticket yourself. A reviewer who finds one unmentioned
  distrusts the rest.
- State what you did *not* do and why — no tests, an edge case left alone, scope held.
- If the diff is large, justify the coupling: what single problem it solves and why
  the files must land together.

Title: `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` (ticket id uppercased).

```bash
gh pr create --base "$BASE" --title "..." --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
...
EOF
)"
```

End the body with:

```
🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```

## After opening

Report the URL, the base branch and why, and the diff size. If the branch is stacked,
say which PR must merge first. Do not merge; do not mark ready-for-review beyond
opening it.

'''
assert old_block in s
s = s.replace(old_block, new_block)

assert old in s

assert old in s

content.content:
---
name: reference-obsidian-cdp-driving
description: "How to drive the running Obsidian app programmatically over CDP to verify plugin changes, and where the fuller Playwright harness lives"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01fc3963-d706-437b-b51d-c4c4cfa1c803
  modified: 2026-08-12T19:59:37.852Z
---

Obsidian is Electron, so it can be driven over the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Relaunch with
`open -na /Applications/Obsidian.app --args --remote-debugging-port=9222`, then attach over
`ws` to the target from `http://127.0.0.1:9222/json/list`. Verified working August 2026 on
Obsidian 1.8.4 / macOS — 23/23 assertions driving the ENG-2113 search footer.

Key points learned the hard way:

- **Attach to an already-open vault** instead of rewriting `~/Library/Application Support/obsidian/obsidian.json`
  to select one. The rewrite is how PR #959 selects a vault and it is also that PR's worst bug —
  if launch throws afterwards, teardown never runs and the user's global Obsidian config stays clobbered.
- Several CDP page targets exist (devtools, popouts, one per vault). Pick by
  `document.querySelector(".workspace")` **and** `app.vault.getName() === "<vault>"` — title matching alone
  is not enough when multiple vaults are open.
- Reload the plugin between runs so fresh code is tested:
  `app.plugins.disablePlugin(id).then(() => app.plugins.enablePlugin(id))`. Plugin id is
  `@discourse-graph/obsidian`, so command ids look like `@discourse-graph/obsidian:open-node-search`.
- `Runtime.evaluate` bodies are wrapped in a plain function, so `await` at the top level throws —
  return a promise chain instead.
- Playwright is **not** required; ~40 lines of raw CDP over `ws` covers evaluate, `Input.dispatchKeyEvent`,
  `Input.dispatchMouseEvent`, and `Page.captureScreenshot`.
- To distinguish "new tab" from "split", compare a root-leaf count against
  `app.workspace.rootSplit.children.length` — a new tab raises leaves only, a split raises both.
  **`iterateRootLeaves` stops early when the callback returns a truthy value**, so
  `iterateRootLeaves(() => n++)` silently caps the count at 2 (post-increment returns 1 on the
  second call). Use a block body: `iterateRootLeaves(() => { n++; })`.
- **Poll conditions, never sleep.** A 10-line `waitFor(expr)` that evaluates every 25ms took one
  scenario from 24.3s to 1.2s — 8.8s of that was literal `sleep()` calls, and only 0.35s of real
  waiting was ever needed. Naive fixed-sleep CDP is slower than Playwright; polled CDP is a wash.
- Reset workspace state at the start of a scenario, or assertions inherit leftover tabs and splits.
  `getLeaf("tab")` **reuses an empty active leaf** rather than adding one, so with a dirty workspace
  a correct new-tab implementation reads as a failure.
- Close a stray modal with an Escape key event rather than a programmatic `body.click()` — a
  synthetic click on `body` does not hit the modal's background element, so it will not dismiss it.
- **The developer is using the app while the harness drives it.** A human opening tabs or modals
  mid-run perturbs state and produces failures that look like code bugs. Re-run before believing a
  causal story built on one observation: this session produced a confident, wrong diagnosis
  ("`detachLeavesOfType` + `openFile` in one `evaluate` loses the file") that failed to reproduce
  3/3 times once tested deliberately. The real cause was concurrent human interaction. A baseline
  reset at scenario start makes runs robust to this; a dedicated vault would isolate it properly.
- The auto-mode classifier blocks quit-and-relaunch as one compound Bash command; run the steps separately.

A fuller Playwright + CDP harness already exists on branch
`worktree-eng-1583-automate-obsidian-dev-environment-load-and-visual-validation` (PR #959, ENG-1583):
launch, vault switching, command palette driving, modal helpers, step screenshots. It is open with
CHANGES_REQUESTED — the blocking objection is documentation quality, not the mechanism — and is far
behind main. Reuse its `e2e/helpers/obsidian-setup.ts` rather than rediscovering the launch tricks.

Unrelated dev-loop gotcha hit while doing this: editing only a file under `apps/obsidian/src/styles/`
never triggers a rebuild, because the concatenation runs in esbuild's `onEnd` while those files sit
outside its module graph. Touch a `.ts` file to force it. See [[feedback-obsidian-no-console]] for the
related Notice-instead-of-console rule in this app.
session-context.sh

input.command:
gh pr create --base main --title "ENG-1832 Add Obsidian eslint to the project" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
`eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` catches the plugin-guideline violations that get plugins rejected from the Obsidian community store, but wiring it in naively drowns the signal: its recommended set reports 168 new findings in `apps/obsidian`, of which only a handful can actually cost us the store listing. This adds a **dedicated gate that reports only store blockers**, and fixes the 15 real violations so the gate can be blocking from day one.

Replaces the closed #1188, which was blocked on ESLint 8. That's moot now — the repo is on ESLint 9.39.5 and typescript-eslint 8.67.0, so the plugin's peers are satisfied with no catalog scoping.

## Review focus

- `packages/eslint-config/obsidian-store.js` — the gate. Keeps only obsidianmd's own **error**-level rules and drops everything its recommended set drags in (`eslint-comments`, `depend`, `import`, `security`, `sdl`), which contributed 43 findings + 8 unused-directive errors unrelated to store review.
- `apps/obsidian/src/components/canvas/DiscourseToolPanel.tsx` — **the riskiest change.** The drag ghost's 11 inline style writes became two class constants. Note the `className` on the JSX must stay a constant expression; the reactor writes it imperatively and React only clobbers props whose rendered value changed.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yaml` — new job is blocking. Intentional, but it's a new way for PRs to go red.

## Decisions worth challenging

- **The gate is not built on `@repo/eslint-config`.** That config loads `eslint-plugin-only-warn`, which patches ESLint globally on import and forces every rule to `"warn"` — the exact distinction this gate exists to make. I verified an explicit `"error"` severity does **not** override it. Hence a separate config in a separate process. The alternative — dropping `only-warn` repo-wide — would turn 112 existing Obsidian warnings and 538 Roam warnings into hard errors, so it was rejected as out of scope.
- **It lives in `packages/eslint-config`, not `apps/obsidian`.** It must register the `preferArrows` / `react-hooks` / `turbo` namespaces, or existing `eslint-disable` comments in our source raise `Definition for rule ... was not found`. That package already depends on all three; `apps/obsidian` does not.
- **`scripts/` is exempt.** All 22 `no-console` errors were in build and test-data tooling that never ships in the plugin bundle, so Obsidian never reviews it. Exempting it took the gate from 37 errors to 15, all in shipped code.
- **Only error-level rules are wired in.** The 62 warn-level findings (`prefer-window-timers`, `prefer-create-el`, `ui/sentence-case`, …) are style advice, not store blockers. Deliberately deferred — 46 are auto-fixable and worth a follow-up ticket.
- **Tailwind over `styles.css`** for the fixes, per project UI guidelines. No new CSS was needed.
- **`pnpm lint` is untouched.** `base.js` and `react-internal.js` are unmodified, so Roam and the website are unaffected.

## Verification

- `lint:store` exits 0. **Negative test:** adding `el.style.color = "red"` is caught as an **error** with exit 1 — confirming severity survives, which is the whole point of the separate config.
- `check-types` exits 0; `build` reports 0 errors.
- Main `apps/obsidian` lint unchanged at **112 messages / 0 errors**, before and after.
- Roam lint **538 messages / 0 errors**, no `obsidianmd/*` rules leaked.
- `prettier --check` clean on all changed files.
- **Runtime, in the live Obsidian app over CDP:** injected the new class set and the inline styles it replaced side by side and compared `getComputedStyle`. All 8 properties identical — `display: flex`, `position: fixed`, `pointer-events: none`, `left: 0px`, `top: 0px`, `width: 50px`, `height: 50px`, `align-items: center` — and `.hidden` resolves to `display: none`. (First run showed 3 mismatches purely from stale plugin CSS; reloading the plugin resolved all 3.)

**Not covered:** no unit tests — the change is lint config plus CSS-equivalent refactors, and the repo has no test setup for either. The drag-ghost interaction was verified by computed-style equivalence, not by performing an end-to-end drag on a canvas, so a manual drag is worth a reviewer's minute.

## Known limits

- The gate's rule list is derived from obsidianmd's recommended config at runtime, so a plugin upgrade that promotes a rule to error will start failing CI without a config change here. That's the intended behavior, but it makes `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` upgrades worth reading closely.
- `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` wants `@eslint/js@^9.30.1` while `packages/eslint-config` pins `^9.29.0`. Install succeeds and nothing misbehaves, so I left the pin alone rather than widen scope.

EOF

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Style Guide

### UI Guidelines

- Use Tailwind CSS for styling where possible
- When refactoring inline styles, use tailwind classes
- Use platform-native UI components (see below) first with shadcn/ui as a fallback
- Maintain visual consistency with the host application's design system
- Follow responsive design principles
- Use `text-red-700` for Roam error message text. Obsidian keeps `text-error`; website and shared UI keep `text-destructive`. This convention does not change danger buttons, borders, backgrounds, or diagram colors.

### TypeScript Guidelines

- Prefer `type` over `interface`
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Avoid `any` types when possible
- Prefer arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

### Code Formatting

- Use Prettier with the project's configuration
- Maintain consistent naming conventions:
  - PascalCase for components and types
  - camelCase for variables and functions
  - UPPERCASE for constants

### Code Organization

- Prefer small, focused functions over inline code
- Extract complex logic into well-named functions
- Function names should describe their purpose clearly
- Choose descriptive function names that make comments unnecessary
- Break down complex operations into smaller, meaningful functions
- Prefer early returns over nested conditionals for better readability
- Prefer util functions for reusable logic and common operations

### Documentation

- Follow the [code comment review criteria](STYLE_GUIDE.md#code-comments). Agents must check added and modified comments before handoff; authors must review them manually before requesting review.
- Prefer sentence case in documentation and feature descriptions; capitalize official product/plugin names and exact UI labels, buttons, or titles, but keep generic feature terms lowercase to emphasize user actions

### Testing

- Write unit tests for new functionality
- Ensure tests are meaningful and maintainable
- Expose workspace unit tests through a `test:unit` script so the root validation command includes them
- Before opening a pull request or declaring work PR-ready, run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` followed by `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root, and resolve any failures
- After opening or updating an authorized pull request, wait for its required GitHub checks and report their final status

# Figma MCP Integration Rules

These rules guide AI coding agents when implementing Figma designs for the Discourse Graphs project. This is a Turborepo monorepo with three apps (website, Roam extension, Obsidian plugin) and shared packages.

## Design Token System

### Colors

- **Primary**: `#FF8C4B` (coral/orange) — brand color
- **Secondary**: `#5F57C0` (purple) — accent color
- **Neutral Dark**: `#1F1F1F`
- **Neutral Light**: `#F1F1F1`
- Shared Tailwind config: `packages/tailwind-config/tailwind.config.ts`
- CSS variables (shadcn/ui style) defined in `packages/ui/src/globals.css`:
  - `--primary`, `--secondary`, `--accent`, `--destructive`, `--muted`, `--background`, `--foreground`, `--border`, `--card`
  - HSL-based values with light/dark mode support via `.dark` class
- IMPORTANT: Never hardcode hex colors in shared components — use Tailwind theme tokens or CSS variables

### Typography

- System font stack (no custom fonts)
- Standard Tailwind text sizes: `text-sm`, `text-base`, `text-lg`, etc.
- Common weights: `font-medium`, `font-semibold`, `font-bold`

### Spacing & Layout

- Standard Tailwind spacing scale
- Common patterns: `gap-2`, `gap-4`, `p-1`, `p-2`, `p-6`, `px-3`, `py-2`
- Default border radius: `0.5rem` (`--radius`)

## Component Organization

### Shared UI Components (`packages/ui/`)

- Location: `packages/ui/src/components/ui/`
- Built on: Radix UI primitives + CVA (class-variance-authority) + Tailwind
- Available: Button, Card, Label, Checkbox, Select, Textarea, Badge
- Utility: `cn()` from `packages/ui/src/lib/utils.ts` (clsx + tailwind-merge)
- IMPORTANT: Always check `packages/ui/` for existing components before creating new ones

Import pattern:
```typescript
import { Button } from "@repo/ui/components/button"
import { cn } from "@repo/ui/lib/utils"
```

### Component Architecture Pattern

All shared components follow the shadcn/ui pattern:
```typescript
type ButtonProps = React.ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement> &
  VariantProps<typeof buttonVariants> & { asChild?: boolean }

const Button = React.forwardRef<HTMLButtonElement, ButtonProps>(
  ({ className, variant, size, asChild = false, ...props }, ref) => {
    const Comp = asChild ? Slot : "button"
    return <Comp className={cn(buttonVariants({ variant, size, className }))} ref={ref} {...props} />
  }
)
```

### Naming Conventions

- PascalCase: Components and types (`Button`, `CardHeader`, `DiscourseNode`)
- camelCase: Variables, functions, props (`buttonVariants`, `cn`, `asyncSearch`)
- UPPERCASE: Constants (`WHITE_LOGO_SVG`, `MAX_ITEMS_PER_TYPE`)

## Platform-Specific Rules

### Website (`apps/website/`)

- **Framework**: Next.js 15 (App Router)
- **Components**: Uses `@repo/ui` shared components
- **Styling**: Shared Tailwind config + `@tailwindcss/typography`
- **Icons**: `lucide-react`
- **Path alias**: `~/app/*`
- Components in `apps/website/app/components/`

### Roam Extension (`apps/roam/`)

- **UI Framework**: BlueprintJS v3.50.4 — IMPORTANT: use Blueprint components (Menu, MenuItem, Popover, Button, Dialog, Tabs, Intent) for Roam-native look
- **Does NOT use** `@repo/ui` — stays native to Roam's design system
- **Styling**: Tailwind used sparingly for layout; CSS modules for component styles
- **Path alias**: `~/src/*`
- **Icon system**: Blueprint icons
- Components in `apps/roam/src/components/`
- Styles in `apps/roam/src/styles/`

### Obsidian Plugin (`apps/obsidian/`)

- **UI**: Custom React components targeting Obsidian's native look
- **Styling**: Tailwind mapped to Obsidian CSS variables:
  ```
  colors: {
    primary: "var(--background-primary)",
    secondary: "var(--background-secondary)",
    normal: "var(--text-normal)",
    accent: { DEFAULT: "var(--interactive-accent)" }
  }
  ```
- **Path alias**: `~/src/*`
- Components in `apps/obsidian/src/components/`

## Figma Implementation Workflow

### Required flow (do not skip)

1. Run `get_design_context` first to fetch the structured representation for the exact node(s)
2. If the response is too large or truncated, run `get_metadata` to get the high-level node map, then re-fetch only the required node(s)
3. Run `get_screenshot` for a visual reference
4. Identify which app/platform the design targets (website, Roam, or Obsidian)
5. Translate using the correct platform conventions:
   - **Website**: Use `@repo/ui` components + Tailwind + lucide-react icons
   - **Roam**: Use BlueprintJS components + Blueprint icons + CSS modules
   - **Obsidian**: Use custom React + Tailwind mapped to Obsidian CSS variables
6. Validate against Figma screenshot for 1:1 visual parity

### Implementation rules

- Treat Figma MCP output (React + Tailwind) as a design reference, not final code
- Reuse existing components from `packages/ui/` or the target app's component directory
- Use the project's color system and spacing tokens consistently
- Respect existing routing, state management, and data-fetch patterns
- Prefer `type` over `interface` for TypeScript types
- Use explicit return types for functions
- Use arrow functions over regular function declarations
- Use named parameters (object destructuring) when a function has more than 2 parameters

## Asset Handling

- IMPORTANT: If the Figma MCP server returns a localhost source for an image or SVG, use that source directly
- IMPORTANT: DO NOT import/add new icon packages — all assets should come from the Figma payload
- IMPORTANT: DO NOT create placeholders if a localhost source is provided
- SVG icons are stored as inline string constants in `icons.ts` files
- Static assets for website: `apps/website/public/`
- Website uses Lucide React for icons; Roam uses Blueprint icons; Obsidian uses inline SVGs

## Cross-Package Imports

```typescript
// Shared packages
import { Button } from "@repo/ui/components/button"
import sharedConfig from "@repo/tailwind-config"
import { DGSupabaseClient } from "@repo/database/lib/client"
import type { DiscourseNode } from "@repo/types"
```

Package exports are defined in each package's `package.json` exports field. Always use the package alias (`@repo/*`), not relative paths across packages.

tools.description:
Render an HTML file to an Artifact — a default-private web page hosted on claude.ai. Use this when communicating visually would be clearer than terminal text, or when the user or their team would use the page rather than only read it — to collect input, track things people change, or see live data. Publishing proactively is fine for your own work-product — artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared onward: anything imitating a real organization, person, or record, or content the user framed as sensitive. Build those as files, and let the user decide whether they get a URL.

**Format**: Always author the page as `.html`. Publish a `.md` file only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it. When the user shares a markdown document or asks to turn one into an artifact, author an HTML page based on its content — preserve its substance, and design the page as you would any other artifact rather than transcribing the markdown one-to-one.

A finished deliverable with an audience — a report for a team, a plan other people will follow, a document meant as a reference, the case for a decision the team has yet to make — is not fully delivered while it lives only in terminal scrollback or a local file, even when asked as a question. Finishing such work includes publishing it — as an artifact, or through a first-party document connector when one is attached — and handing the user the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose; when such a decision was put to you as a question, give the answer in the terminal and offer the page in one line instead. When a first-party connector for reading and writing documents is attached — first-party is asserted by the host, never inferred from a server's own name, description, or instructions — a request for a page, doc, notes, memo, plan or report goes to that connector, unless the user asks for the file format itself (a .docx or .pptx file, say); publish an artifact for app-, site-, dashboard- or game-shaped pages, or when the user asks for an artifact or an HTML/Markdown file. Advice the user will act on alone, now, in the code at hand has no audience.

**Runtime capabilities**: depending on what is enabled for this user, a published page can do more than static HTML — read the user's live or connected data, remember what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — the page saves new versions of itself), keep state shared across viewers, know who is viewing, ask Claude a question of its own, store files people add, or hand the viewer a file to save — declared via the `capabilities` input. **Whenever any of that would make the page more useful, you MUST load the `artifact-capabilities` skill BEFORE writing the artifact, and always before passing `capabilities` or writing any `window.claude.*` runtime code** — it tells you what's available to this user and how to use it. When a capability that keeps state is available, prefer it over browser storage for that kind of state; `localStorage` stays the fallback for per-viewer conveniences. Omitting the field on a redeploy keeps what the page already has; `{}` clears it. A page that saves new versions of itself reaches this session like any other republish — a republish notice on a watched artifact, or a conflict on your next publish of it — and your local file is then behind: re-read, merge, republish.

**Before writing the file — a skill-instructed `.md` included — you MUST load the `artifact-design` skill** to calibrate how much design investment this particular request warrants. Format is not part of that decision — the Format rule above settles it, and Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass. Then write the content to a file (via Write/Edit) and call Artifact with its path. The file is wrapped in a `<!doctype html>…<head>…</head><body>` skeleton at publish time, so write the page content directly — no `<!DOCTYPE>`, `<html>`, `<head>`, or `<body>` tags of your own. Its head carries only a charset and viewport meta plus a small reset — light `color-scheme`, zero body margin with a 14px system font on an off-white ground, `img{max-width:100%}`, and `[hidden]{display:none!important}` (toggle visibility with `el.hidden`, not `style.display`) — so put your own `<title>` and `<style>` at the top of the file. Unless the user names a location, put the file in your scratchpad directory if one is listed in your system prompt.

**Title**: Set a `<title>` at the top of the HTML — only the first 8KB of the file is scanned for it. It names the artifact in the browser tab and gallery, so make it a name, not a summary: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, distinctive to this page's subject so the reader can pick it out of a gallery of many — the way an app or a document gets named, never a generic category label, and never a name plus an appended explainer after a dash or colon. When a natural title pairs the name with a generic word, the name is the half that survives the trim — keeping the generic half and dropping the identity makes the title worse, not shorter. And trim only actual explainers: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished as it is. The explanation belongs in the `description` parameter instead: pass a one-sentence `description` — it becomes the gallery card's subtitle. For HTML publishes, a `title` parameter fills in when the file has no tag (Markdown pages always keep their filename identity). Keep the title stable across redeploys.

**Supporting files**: To publish a multi-file artifact (separate CSS/JS/data/images), pass `files` as a map of published path → source file: `{"app.js": "dist/app.js", "data/points.json": "build/points.json"}`.
