tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

input.description: Research Obsidian automated review
input.prompt:
Research ONLY official Obsidian sources. Do NOT look at the eslint-plugin-obsidianmd npm package or its repo (another agent covers that).

Question: What automated checks does Obsidian run on community plugin submissions and releases as of late 2026?

Investigate these sources specifically:
1. github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-releases — the repo where plugin submissions are PRs. Look at .github/workflows/ and any validation scripts. What bot/action runs? What does it check?
2. docs.obsidian.md — "Submit your plugin", "Plugin guidelines", "Releasing" pages. Any mention of an automated validator, "source review", or an ESLint-based bot.
3. Obsidian forum / official announcements about an automated plugin review bot, especially anything from 2026.

Specific things I need answered:
- Is there an automated "source code review" step that reports ERRORS with file:line references to plugin authors? The user saw a UI panel titled "SOURCE CODE" listing errors like "Unexpected undescribed directive comment. Include descriptions to explain why the comment is necessary. src/components/useSchemaSelection.ts:117" and "Creating and attaching "style" elements is not allowed. For loading CSS, use a "styles.css" file instead, which Obsidian loads for you. src/utils/tagNodeHandler.ts:120"
- Where does that UI live? Is it a GitHub check, a bot comment, or a web dashboard for plugin authors?
- What tool powers it?
- There was also an error "Source review dependency installation failed — Checks which require resolved dependencies were skipped. Scan results are incomplete until dependencies can be installed." What does this mean, what does the reviewer try to run (npm install? yarn?), and does it struggle with pnpm monorepos?
- Can plugin authors run these checks locally? Is there a published CLI or GitHub Action?

Report concrete findings with URLs. Distinguish clearly between what you verified from a primary source and what you are inferring. If you cannot confirm something, say so explicitly rather than guessing.

content.text:
The local evidence is decisive, and I need to own a significant error.

## You were right — and I built the gate backwards

Running obsidianmd's **full** `recommended` config against your code reproduces both screenshot errors at the exact file and line:

| Screenshot | Reproduced locally |
|---|---|
| `useSchemaSelection.ts:117` — undescribed directive comment | ✅ `eslint-comments/require-description` |
| `tagNodeHandler.ts:120` — style elements not allowed | ✅ `obsidianmd/no-forbidden-elements` |

That's not coincidence. Obsidian's automated source review is running this rule set.

**Two things I got wrong:**

1. **I filtered the gate to `obsidianmd/*` rules only** and stripped the bundled plugins — `eslint-comments`, `depend`, `import`, `security`, `sdl` — calling them "43 findings unrelated to store review." Your first error is `eslint-comments/require-description`, one of the rules I threw away. There are **27** of those in your code.

2. **I called `tagNodeHandler.ts:120` a likely false positive.** Obsidian reports it as an Error. My reasoning about popout windows may still explain *why* the code is written that way, but it doesn't make the finding go away.

The consequence is the bad kind: **my gate reports 16 errors and passes CI, while the real review fails you.** False confidence is worse than no gate.

| | Errors |
|---|---|
| My gate (`obsidianmd/*` only) | 16 |
| Full `recommended` (what review appears to run) | **161** |

## The third line matters too

> *Source review dependency installation failed — Checks which require resolved dependencies were skipped. Scan results are incomplete until dependencies can be installed.*

Your scan **did not complete**. Type-aware rules were skipped, so the two errors shown are only what survived. That's consistent with what I see locally: most of the 161 come from `@typescript-eslint` rules needing type information, which is exactly what gets skipped when install fails.

So the real number for v1.7.0 is likely well above two. This is probably because `apps/obsidian` is a pnpm workspace package — the reviewer clones the repo and runs a plain install, which won't resolve `workspace:*` deps like `@repo/database` and `@repo/utils`.

That's arguably the more urgent finding: **fix the dependency install and you'll see many more errors than you do now.**

I have two research agents verifying the official mechanism — whether this is definitively `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd`, where that UI lives, and whether there's a published CLI or Action to run it locally. I'll report when they land rather than guess.

Meanwhile the PR needs rework: the gate should run the **full** recommended set, not my filtered subset. I'd hold off merging #1328 as-is.

  **Discrepancy worth knowing**: `docs/configuration.md` says "Only security-critical rules remain at `error`: `no-eval`, `no-implied-eval`, `no-unsanitized/method`, `no-unsanitized/property`, `obsidianmd/regex-lookbehind`, and `obsidianmd/no-forbidden-elements`" and its "Full scanner-equivalent configuration" snippet **omits the eslint-comments rules entirely**. That doc section is incomplete relative to the actual scanner config in obsidian-workflows. Treat the doc as the less reliable of the two.
  
  ---
  
  ## 4. `obsidianmd/no-forbidden-elements` — ERROR, and no exception exists
  
  **Verified error severity in review.** docs/configuration.md lists it among the six rules that "remain at `error`", and `obsidian-workflows/src/lint.ts` sets `"obsidianmd/no-forbidden-elements": "error"` explicitly after the `toWarns()` pass. PR #173 also lists it under "Rules kept at `error` (scanner re-escalates these)".
  
  **No documented exception.** Verified from `lib/rules/noForbiddenElements.ts`: `schema: []` — the rule takes **no options at all**. The message you saw is messageId `doNotAttachForbiddenStyleElements`:
  > `Creating and attaching "{{element}}" elements is not allowed. For loading CSS, use a "styles.css" file instead, which Obsidian loads for you.`
  
  Forbidden tags are exactly `["link", "style"]`. The rule fires on the *creation* call, regardless of whether anything is ever attached.
  
  **The false-positive discussion exists and was NOT resolved in the developer's favour.** Issue #197, "no-forbidden-elements: legitimate runtime use cases for dynamic `<style>` elements" (https://github.com/obsidianmd/eslint-plugin/issues/197), filed by zsviczian (Excalidraw), argues exactly the per-user/per-operation generated-CSS case:
  
  > "`setCssProps()` / `setCssStyles()` are not equivalent when the requirement is a stylesheet rather than declarations on a single element. They cannot express selectors, pseudo-elements, at-rules, or arbitrary rule text."
  
  He asked for either "a narrowly scoped, documented exception" or "an Obsidian-supported pattern for lifecycle-owned runtime stylesheets". Maintainer saberzero1's answer was to point at the **constructable `CSSStyleSheet` API** as the sanctioned alternative ("the exact use-case for this"). The reporter's counter was that Obsidian still supports iOS 15, where adopted stylesheets are unavailable, so a `<style>` fallback must remain and would still be flagged. **The issue was closed by the reporter himself (not by a maintainer), state_reason `completed`, with no code change and no exception added.** So: no exception shipped, and the maintainer position is "use CSSStyleSheet".
  
  **Popout windows specifically: nothing documented, and I found no issue about it.** Related-but-different open issue #196, "prefer-create-el: iframe contentDocument has no Obsidian DOM helper equivalent" (https://github.com/obsidianmd/eslint-plugin/issues/196), covers the sibling problem of a *foreign document* having no Obsidian helper — that is the closest analogue to the popout case and it is still open.
  
  **Inference (my reading of the rule source, not documented anywhere)**: the detector for `createElement` requires the callee object to be the literal identifier `document`:
  ```js
  node.callee.object.type === Identifier && node.callee.object.name === "document"
  ```
  so `popoutWin.document.createElement("style")` or `activeDocument.createElement("style")` would **not** match, whereas `anything.createEl("style")` **would** (the `createEl` branch accepts Identifier *or* MemberExpression objects). That is a real escape hatch in today's implementation, but it is an artifact rather than a sanctioned exception and could be tightened at any time — I would not build on it without a described `eslint-disable` as backup.
  
  ---
  
  ## 5. Running the same rule set locally — yes, two options, both official
  
  **(a) Documented config, in the repo.** `docs/configuration.md` → "Community plugin scanner configuration" → collapsible "Full scanner-equivalent configuration" gives a copy-pasteable `eslint.config.mjs` with the scanner's `globalIgnores([...])` list and rule overrides. Caveat stated in the doc itself:
  > "Note: The actual scanner also downgrades all non-security rule severities from `error` to `warn`. The configuration above does not replicate that behavior… If you want identical severity levels, you would need to override each rule individually."
  
  It also notes up front: "You do not need to replicate this configuration… This section is provided for transparency."
  
  **(b) The official GitHub Action — closer to exact.** `obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows` (https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows), described as:
  > "A GitHub Action that validates, lints, builds, and releases Obsidian plugins and themes. Matches the community directory's validation and scanner expectations so your submissions pass on the first try."
  
  Usage: `- uses: obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows@v1` in a PR workflow. Its `src/lint.ts` writes a temporary `eslint.config.scanner.mjs` and pins the scanner toolchain:
  ```js
  const SCANNER_ESLINT_DEPS = { eslint: '9.37.0', 'eslint-plugin-obsidianmd': '0.4.1', 'typescript-eslint': '8.61.1' }
  ```
  (worth noting: the action pins **0.4.1**, matching the version in your context — that is very likely the version behind the review panel output you saw.)
  
  Its generated config, verbatim in essence: `toWarns(obsidianmd.configs.recommended)` with eslint-comments exempted from the downgrade, then errors for `no-eval`, `no-implied-eval`, `no-unsanitized/method`, `no-unsanitized/property`, `obsidianmd/regex-lookbehind`, `obsidianmd/no-forbidden-elements`; offs for `no-undef`, the `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-*` family (later re-added at `warn`), `restrict-template-expressions`, `no-base-to-string`, `import/no-unresolved`, `validate-manifest`, `validate-license`, `commands/no-command-in-command-id`, `commands/no-plugin-id-in-command-id`, all three `ui/sentence-case*`; and error re-escalations for `settings-tab/no-manual-html-headings`, `settings-tab/no-problematic-settings-headings`, `sample-names`, `no-sample-code`, `platform`, `no-plugin-as-component`, `detach-leaves`, `no-static-styles-assignment`, `no-view-references-in-plugin`, `no-unsupported-api`. It sets `noInlineConfig: false` and `reportUnusedDisableDirectives: "off"` / `reportUnusedInlineConfigs: "off"` — i.e. in *this* mirror, inline `eslint-disable` comments are honoured.
  
  **Cannot confirm**: whether the production review bot is literally this action's code path or a separate service that this action merely approximates. The README only claims it "matches… expectations". Several open issues (#178 "Scorecard reports warnings on non-plugin code", #182 "Community dashboard reports mass unsafe-type false positives when dependencies are unresolved") report the real scanner behaving differently from local runs — notably running type-checked rules without `node_modules` resolved, and #178 reporting that repo-level `ignores` and per-file rule overrides did **not** change the scorecard. So repo-level config exemptions may not reach the real bot even though the mirror honours them. Treat "local run == review output" as approximate.
  
  There is a `bin` entry `eslint-plugin-obsidian` → `dist/lib/index.js` in package.json, but that file is the plugin module, not a CLI; there is no standalone CLI and no `action.yml` in the eslint-plugin repo itself.
  
  ---
  
  ## 6. What changed in 0.3.x and 0.4.x (from GitHub release notes)
  
  There is no CHANGELOG.md in the repo (PR #188 "docs: added changelog" is still open). Release notes:
  
  **0.3.0** (2026-05-12) — `prefer-active-doc` **disabled by default** (PR #137); sentence-case rule disabled ("not working as intended"); Cursor added to recognized brands; fixes for `.obsidian` in URLs, `createDocumentFragment` on `activeDocument`, active-window rules.
  
  **0.4.0** (2026-06-30) — the big one. `obsidianmd/no-nodejs-modules` replaces `import/no-nodejs-modules`; new rules `settings-tab/prefer-setting-definitions` and `settings-tab/no-deprecated-display` (PR #161, by liamcain); type-only `moment` imports allowed; documentation integrated into rules; rules properly scoped to file types; and **PR #173 "Community scanners ruleset"** — the breaking severity realignment described above (most rules dropped from `error` to `warn` to match the scanner's `toWarns()`, ~13 kept/re-escalated to `error`, and the four `eslint-comments/*` rules + `reportUnusedDisableDirectives` added at `error`). PR #173's own wording: *"**Breaking**: Rules that were `error` are now `warn` for non-escalated rules… Projects with `/* eslint-disable */` comments without descriptions or without matching re-enables will now see `eslint-comments/*` errors."*
  
  **0.4.1** (2026-07-02) — single fix: "wrong `activeDocument.createEl()` calls" (PR #174).
  
  **0.4.2** (2026-08-24) — new `ruleConfigs.recommended` / `ruleConfigs.recommendedTypeChecked` exports (obsidianmd rule presets as plain rule objects, usable without the full recommended config); new `docs/configuration.md` including the community-plugin-scanner section; README moved to `projectService` + `allowDefaultProject`; legacy `.eslintrc` docs removed.
  
  ---
  
  ## Practical upshot for the DG Obsidian plugin
  
  1. `eslint-comments/require-description` errors are trivially fixable — append ` -- <reason>` to every disable comment. Note `eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable` also errors on disabling `obsidianmd/*`, `no-console`, `no-eval`, `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` and others, so a described disable of an `obsidianmd/*` rule will *still* error.
  2. `no-forbidden-elements` for per-user CSS / popout windows has no sanctioned exception. The maintainer-endorsed path is constructable `CSSStyleSheet` (`new CSSStyleSheet()` + `doc.adoptedStyleSheets`), which also works for a popout window's own document. If a `<style>` fallback must stay, expect the finding to persist; issue #197 is the precedent and it ended without relief.
  3. To reproduce review locally, prefer adding `obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows@v1` as a CI job over hand-copying the doc's config snippet — the snippet explicitly does not replicate severities.

content.content:
# Obsidian Workflows GitHub Action

## Purpose
This action "validates, lints, builds, and releases Obsidian plugins and themes" to match community directory standards.

## Minimal CI YAML for Plugin Linting

```yaml
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, master]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows@v1
```

The action automatically detects whether your project is a plugin or theme.

## Available Inputs

| Input | Default | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `type` | `auto` | Specify project type: `plugin`, `theme`, or `auto` |
| `mode` | `pr` | Execution mode: `pr` (CI checks) or `release` |
| `build` | _(empty)_ | Override the build command; set to `false` to skip |
| `lint` | `true` | Enable/disable linting |
| `scanner-lint` | `false` | Use community scanner lint rules instead of project config |
| `strict` | `false` | Fail on policy findings (default treats as warnings) |
| `node-version` | `24` | Node.js version (minimum: 20) |

## Monorepo Support

The documentation provided does not mention support for plugins in subdirectories or working-directory configuration options. There is no indication this action handles monorepo structures with plugins in non-root paths.

content.text:
Confirmed from primary sources. Here's the full picture.

## Yes — it is `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd`

From the plugin's own `docs/configuration.md`:

> "The Obsidian community plugin directory runs this plugin against every submitted plugin as part of its automated review."

The panel you saw lives at `community.obsidian.md/account/plugins/<id>` — the new directory that replaced the `obsidian-releases` PR flow. Errors there **block installability**, and per Obsidian's bot-filed issues, existing entries are informational only **until October 30, 2026** (that date appears in bot issues and press, not on docs.obsidian.md — treat as likely, not certain). That's a month away.

## The mismatch was mine, and it's the bulk of your errors

The scanner runs the **full** `recommended` config, then applies a severity transform: most rules drop to warning, but `eslint-comments/*` stays at **error**, along with the security rules and ~10 re-escalated `obsidianmd/*` rules.

I filtered the gate to `obsidianmd/*` and discarded `eslint-comments` as "unrelated noise." Applying the scanner's actual transform to your code:

| Rule | Count |
|---|---|
| `eslint-comments/require-description` | 25 |
| `obsidianmd/no-static-styles-assignment` | 15 |
| `eslint-comments/disable-enable-pair` | 12 |
| `eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable` | 1 |
| `obsidianmd/no-forbidden-elements` | 1 |
| **Total blocking** | **54** |

My gate reports **16**. **37 of the 54 — 69% — are the `eslint-comments` rules I threw away.**

Concentrated in a few files: `relationUtils.tsx` (28), `DiscourseToolPanel.tsx` (11), `DiscourseRelationBinding.tsx` (6).

The good news: the 37 `eslint-comments` ones are nearly mechanical — append ` -- reason` to each disable comment.

**Also: my suggested fix for `tagNodeHandler.ts` was wrong.** `eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable` bans disabling `obsidianmd/*` rules, so a suppression there would itself error. Issue #197 raised exactly your popout/dynamic-CSS argument and closed with no exception; the maintainer's sanctioned answer is constructable `CSSStyleSheet` + `doc.adoptedStyleSheets` — which also solves the popout case properly.

One thing I had right: `scripts/` really is in the scanner's ignore list.

## Your dependency failure is a known monorepo bug

> *Source review dependency installation failed*

This is [forum thread 116176](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/bug-plugin-scorecard-linter-cannot-resolve-internal-deps-in-monorepos/116176) — the scanner doesn't build or link internal workspace packages, so `@repo/database` and `@repo/utils` don't resolve. Acknowledged on Discord, no fix shipped.

So your v1.7.0 scan is **incomplete** — type-aware rules were skipped. The 54 above assumes types resolve. Until install is fixed you're flying blind, and when it *is* fixed you may get a flood of false-positive `no-unsafe-*` findings instead.

## What you can run

**1. Official Action** — `obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows@v1`, which "matches the community directory's validation and scanner expectations":

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v7
- uses: obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows@v1
  with:
    scanner-lint: true
```

Caveat: its docs show **no working-directory or subdirectory input**, so pointing it at `apps/obsidian` may not work out of the box. Needs testing.

**2. "Review branch"** on your dashboard entry — runs a real scan against any branch/tag/SHA without cutting a release. This is the only way to reproduce the sandbox's install behavior exactly, and the fastest way to find out whether the monorepo issue is what broke your scan.

## Where that leaves #1328

The PR as it stands gives false confidence — it would have passed your v1.7.0. I'd not merge it. Three ways forward:

start = s.index("## Plugin Store Guidelines")
end = s.index("The rules below are what that gate enforces, plus guidance it cannot check.")
new = """## Plugin Store Guidelines

The Obsidian community directory scans every release with
`eslint-plugin-obsidianmd`, and its errors block the plugin from being
installable. Run the same rules before opening a PR:

```
pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint:scanner
```

This is deliberately separate from `pnpm lint`. The shared repo config loads
`eslint-plugin-only-warn`, which forces every rule to "warn", so scanner
findings would be indistinguishable from style advice. `lint:scanner` runs in
its own process against the plugin's `recommended` set with the directory's
ignore list. Note it is stricter than the real scan, which downgrades most rules
to warnings and keeps only a subset at error.

The authoritative check is the directory itself: use **Review branch** on the
entry's management page at community.obsidian.md to scan any branch without
cutting a release. Obsidian also publishes `obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows` as a
GitHub Action that mirrors the scanner.

CI runs `lint:scanner` through reviewdog, so a finding on a line your PR adds
fails the build; pre-existing ones are reported but tolerated.

"""
p.write_text(s[:start] + new + s[end:])
PY

new = """## Plugin Store Guidelines

The Obsidian community directory scans every release with
`eslint-plugin-obsidianmd`, and its errors block the plugin from being
installable. Run the same rules before opening a PR:

```
pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint:scanner
```

This is deliberately separate from `pnpm lint`. The shared repo config loads
`eslint-plugin-only-warn`, which forces every rule to "warn", so scanner
findings would be indistinguishable from style advice. `lint:scanner` runs in
its own process against the plugin's `recommended` set with the directory's
ignore list. Note it is stricter than the real scan, which downgrades most rules
to warnings and keeps only a subset at error.

The authoritative check is the directory itself: use **Review branch** on the
entry's management page at community.obsidian.md to scan any branch without
cutting a release. Obsidian also publishes `obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows` as a
GitHub Action that mirrors the scanner.

CI runs `lint:scanner` through reviewdog, so a finding on a line your PR adds
fails the build; pre-existing ones are reported but tolerated.

"""
p.write_text(s[:start] + new + s[end:])

git commit -q --amend -F - <<'EOF'
ENG-1832 Add Obsidian eslint to the project

The Obsidian community directory scans every plugin release with
eslint-plugin-obsidianmd, and its errors block the plugin from being
installable. Run the same rules locally and in CI.

Adds `lint:scanner`, which runs the plugin's recommended set with the
directory's documented ignore list in its own process. It needs a
separate config because @repo/eslint-config loads eslint-plugin-only-warn,
which patches ESLint globally on import and forces every rule to "warn".
The subset the scanner keeps at error is also registered in the app's
eslint.config.mjs so editors surface it.

`lint:scanner` is stricter than the real scan, which downgrades most rules
to warnings. Mirroring that transform is not currently practical:
eslint-plugin-obsidianmd 0.4.2 ships a misspelled core rule and blocks
that apply rules whose plugin they do not declare, both of which only
surface once the config is transformed.

CI runs it through reviewdog with filter-mode=added, so the existing
findings are reported without blocking while newly added ones fail.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git push --force-with-lease 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
Reworked and pushed. CI green, `MERGEABLE`.

## What changed

`lint:store` → **`lint:scanner`**, now running the plugin's **full `recommended`** set with the directory's documented ignore list, instead of my hand-picked `obsidianmd/*` subset.

| | Findings surfaced |
|---|---|
| Old gate | 16 |
| New `lint:scanner` | 126 errors, 92 warnings |
| Visible in your editor | 0 → **58** |

The 37 `eslint-comments/*` errors that caused your v1.7.0 failure — and that my version discarded entirely — now show up.

## One compromise you should know about

I could not faithfully mirror the scanner's severity transform, and I tried hard. The real scanner downgrades most rules to warnings and keeps ~20 at error. Reproducing that means transforming obsidianmd's config, which exposes two upstream defects:

- `recommended` contains a **misspelled core rule**, `no-prototype-bultins` — still broken in 0.4.2, which I upgraded to while testing
- Config blocks apply `@typescript-eslint` rules without declaring the plugin, which crashes on `package.json` once anything forces validation

Untransformed, it works. So `lint:scanner` is a **superset** — stricter than the real scan, never laxer. It will flag things the directory only warns about. Given the alternative was silently missing 69% of your blocking errors, I'd rather err strict, but it's a real cost and worth revisiting if upstream fixes those bugs.

## Two things I'd treat as more urgent than this PR

**1. The dependency-install failure.** Your v1.7.0 scan said *"Source review dependency installation failed — checks which require resolved dependencies were skipped."* That's [a known scanner bug with pnpm workspaces](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/bug-plugin-scorecard-linter-cannot-resolve-internal-deps-in-monorepos/116176) — it can't resolve `@repo/database` or `@repo/utils`. **Your scan is incomplete**, so the two errors you saw may not be all of them. Running **Review branch** on your directory entry is the only way to find out.

**2. The date.** Per Obsidian's bot-filed issues, existing entries are informational only until **October 30, 2026** — about a month out. After that a failing release is delisted. That date comes from bot issues and press, not docs.obsidian.md, so treat it as likely rather than confirmed.

## Also worth correcting

My earlier suggestion to suppress `tagNodeHandler.ts:120` with an `eslint-disable` would itself have errored — `eslint-comments/no-restricted-disable` bans disabling `obsidianmd/*`. The sanctioned fix is constructable `CSSStyleSheet` + `adoptedStyleSheets`, which also handles the popout-window case properly. Issue #197 raised your exact dynamic-CSS argument and closed with no exception granted.

Your `console.log("isInside")` is still uncommitted and out of the PR. Want me to file the two follow-up tickets — the 54 blocking findings, and the monorepo scan failure?

Found it — and it's an exact match, not an approximation.

## The scanner never looked at your `.tsx` files

Splitting my `lint:scanner` findings by extension, counting only rules the scanner treats as errors:

| | Error-level findings |
|---|---|
| `.ts` files | **2** |
| `.tsx` files | **52** |

The two `.ts` findings are:

```
src/components/useSchemaSelection.ts:117  eslint-comments/require-description
src/utils/tagNodeHandler.ts:120           obsidianmd/no-forbidden-elements
```

Those are **exactly** the two errors in your panel. Two of two, same files, same lines. Every one of the 52 findings in `.tsx` files is missing from the report.

## Answering your actual question

**The scanner checks the entire repo, not a diff.** Every release is scanned in full — that's why the FAQ documents a path-based ignore list rather than a diff range, and why "Review branch" scans a whole branch.

So the discrepancy isn't scope. **Your scan didn't finish**, exactly as the third line says:

> *Checks which require resolved dependencies were skipped. Scan results are incomplete until dependencies can be installed.*

Without `node_modules`, `typescript-eslint` can't build a TypeScript program. My reading is that `.tsx` files then fail to parse — JSX support comes from the tsconfig the scanner couldn't resolve — so they're skipped silently. The two survivors are both `.ts`, both from rules that need no type information: a comment-syntax rule and a `createEl("style")` call-shape rule.

That's a hypothesis for the *mechanism*; the *pattern* is not in doubt given 2-for-2.

## What this means for you

Your v1.7.0 result of "2 errors" is **not** a measure of how close you are to passing. Fix the dependency install and the number should jump to roughly **54** — with 52 of them in `.tsx` files that have never been evaluated, concentrated in `relationUtils.tsx` (28), `DiscourseToolPanel.tsx` (11), and `DiscourseRelationBinding.tsx` (6).

This reframes priority. The dependency failure isn't a side issue next to the two errors — it's the thing hiding 96% of your problem. And it's the [known pnpm-workspace limitation](https://forum.obsidian.md/t/bug-plugin-scorecard-linter-cannot-resolve-internal-deps-in-monorepos/116176): the scanner can't resolve `@repo/database` or `@repo/utils`.

It also validates the PR as it now stands. `lint:scanner` sees all 54 because it runs with your real `node_modules`, so it tells you what a *working* scan would say — which the directory currently cannot.

One caveat worth holding: the forum thread reports that once internal deps *do* resolve, the scanner can instead emit a flood of false-positive `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-*` findings. So fixing the install may trade 52 hidden real findings for a mix of real and spurious ones. Running **Review branch** is the cheap way to find out before your next release.

Want me to dig into making the scanner resolve the workspace deps — that's the highest-leverage thing left, and it's a different problem from the lint config.

# Community Plugin Scanner Configuration

The Obsidian community plugin directory runs automated reviews using a modified version of the recommended config. Here's the scanner-equivalent setup:

```js
// eslint.config.mjs
import { defineConfig, globalIgnores } from "eslint/config";
import obsidianmd from "eslint-plugin-obsidianmd";

export default defineConfig([
  {
    languageOptions: {
      parserOptions: {
        projectService: {
          allowDefaultProject: ["eslint.config.*", "manifest.json"],
        },
        extraFileExtensions: [".json"],
      },
    },
  },

  ...obsidianmd.configs.recommended,

  {
    files: ["**/*.{ts,cts,mts,tsx,js,cjs,mjs,jsx}"],
    rules: {
      // Security — keep as errors
      "no-eval": "error",
      "no-implied-eval": "error",
      "no-unsanitized/method": "error",
      "no-unsanitized/property": "error",
      "obsidianmd/regex-lookbehind": "error",
      "obsidianmd/no-forbidden-elements": "error",

      // Covered by TypeScript or too noisy
      "no-undef": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-member-access": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-assignment": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-argument": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-call": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-return": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/restrict-template-expressions": "off",
      "@typescript-eslint/no-base-to-string": "off",
      "import/no-unresolved": "off",

      // Scanner handles these separately
      "obsidianmd/validate-manifest": "off",
      "obsidianmd/validate-license": "off",

      // Old plugins should not change their command ids
      "obsidianmd/commands/no-command-in-command-id": "off",
      "obsidianmd/commands/no-plugin-id-in-command-id": "off",
    },
  },

  globalIgnores([
    "node_modules",
    "dist",
    "build",
    "pkg",
    "test-vault",
    ".obsidian",
    "**/.obsidian/**",
    "esbuild.config.mjs",
    "version-bump.mjs",
    "**/*.test.*",
    "**/*.tests.*",
    "**/*.spec.*",
    "**/*.specs.*",
    "**/test/**",
    "**/tests/**",
    "**/__tests__/**",
    "**/mocks/**",
    "**/__mocks__/**",
    "**/*.cjs",
    "**/*.mjs",
    "**/*.cts",
    "**/*.mts",
    "**/vite*",
    "**/scripts/**",
    "**/docs/**",
    "**/i18n/**",
    "**/i18next/**",
    "**/locale/**",
    "**/locales/**",
    "**/translations/**",
    "**/l10n/**",
    ".pnpm-store",
    "**/*.spec.ts",
    "**/testUtils**",
    "automation/**",
    "e2e-tests/**",
  ]),
]);
```

The actual scanner adjusts non-security rule severities from error to warning, though the configuration above maintains the recommended defaults with only specific rule adjustments.

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues. For PRs over 400 changed lines, excluding tests, include a concise split justification, main review entry points, and testing path in Reviewer brief.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Required standards

- Read and follow [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md) and the nested `AGENTS.md` files that apply to changed files before editing or reviewing code.
- Follow [PR_GUIDELINES.md](PR_GUIDELINES.md) for scope, verification, and review requirements. General code standards live in the style guide; app-specific instructions remain in nested `AGENTS.md` files.
- Before handoff or requesting review, run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` from `.agents/skills/dg-pr-adherence-check/SKILL.md` against the final diff and available PR metadata. Resolve findings or report them explicitly, including missing evidence. Rerun affected checks after changes.

content.content: @AGENTS.md

You are working on the Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

## Dependencies

Prefer existing dependencies from package.json.

## Obsidian Style Guide

Use the obsidian style guide from help.obsidian.md/style-guide and docs.obsidian.md/Developer+policies.

### Icons

Platform-native UI.
Lucide and custom Obsidian icons can be used alongside detailed elements to provide a visual representation of a feature.

Example: In the ribbon on the left, select Create new canvas ( lucide-layout-dashboard.svg > icon ) to create a canvas in the same folder as the active file.

Guidelines for icons

Store icons in the Attachments/icons folder.
Add the prefix lucide- before the Lucide icon name.
Add the prefix obsidian-icon- before the Obsidian icon name.
Example: The icon for creating a new canvas should be named lucide-layout-dashboard.

Use the SVG version of the icons available.
Icons should be 18 pixels in width, 18 pixels in height, and have a stroke width of 1.5. You can adjust these settings in the SVG data.
Adjusting size and stroke in an SVG.
Utilize the icon anchor in embedded images, to tweak the spacing around the icon so that it aligns neatly with the text in the vicinity.
Icons should be surrounded by parenthesis. ( lucide-cog.svg > icon )
Example: ( ![[lucide-cog.svg#icon]] )

### Function guides

- Any function that deals with querying vault's frontmatter, default to using Datacore API first, then write fallback where you use `plugin.app.vault.getMarkdownFiles()` to iterate through each file's frontmatter

## Plugin Store Guidelines

The Obsidian community directory scans every release with
`eslint-plugin-obsidianmd`, and its errors block the plugin from being
installable. Run the same rules before opening a PR:

```
pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint:scanner
```

This is deliberately separate from `pnpm lint`. The shared repo config loads
`eslint-plugin-only-warn`, which forces every rule to "warn", so scanner
findings would be indistinguishable from style advice. `lint:scanner` runs in
its own process against the plugin's `recommended` set with the directory's
ignore list. Note it is stricter than the real scan, which downgrades most rules
to warnings and keeps only a subset at error.

The authoritative check is the directory itself: use **Review branch** on the
entry's management page at community.obsidian.md to scan any branch without
cutting a release. Obsidian also publishes `obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows` as a
GitHub Action that mirrors the scanner.

CI runs `lint:scanner` through reviewdog, so a finding on a line your PR adds
fails the build; pre-existing ones are reported but tolerated.

The rules below are what that gate enforces, plus guidance it cannot check.

These rules must be followed for the plugin to be accepted into the Obsidian community plugin store.

### Security

- Never use `innerHTML`, `outerHTML`, or `insertAdjacentHTML` with user-controlled content
- Use Obsidian DOM helpers instead: `createEl()`, `createDiv()`, `createSpan()`

### App instance

- Always use `this.app` — never the global `app` object

### Event listeners

- Register all event listeners via `this.registerEvent()` so they are automatically cleaned up on plugin unload

### UI text

- Use sentence case in settings headings and labels (not title case)
- Prefer `setHeading()` over raw HTML heading elements (`<h1>`, `<h2>`, etc.)

### Commands

- Do not set default hotkeys — they conflict with other plugins
- Use the correct callback type: `callback` for always-available commands, `checkCallback` when the command is conditionally available, or the editor variants for editor-scoped commands
- Do not manually prepend the plugin ID to command IDs — Obsidian adds it automatically

### Workspace

- Do not store references to custom views — look them up fresh each time they are needed
  Don't do this:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => this.view = new MyCustomView());`
  Do this instead:
  `this.registerView(MY_VIEW_TYPE, () => new MyCustomView());`
  To access the view from your plugin, use `Workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType():`

```
for (let leaf of app.workspace.getActiveLeavesOfType(MY_VIEW_TYPE)) {
  let view = leaf.view;
  if (view instanceof MyCustomView) {
    // ...
  }
}
```

- Do not detach leaves during plugin unload

### Editor

- Prefer the Editor API over `Vault.modify()` when the note is currently open in the editor
- Prefer `Vault.process()` instead of `Vault.modify()` to modify a file in the background

### Mobile compatibility

- Node.js and Electron APIs (`fs`, `crypto`, `os`) are unavailable on mobile
- If the plugin targets mobile, use web API equivalents: `SubtleCrypto` instead of `crypto`, `navigator.clipboard` for clipboard access
- Regex lookbehind assertions are not supported on some mobile — avoid them if possible

### Code quality

- Use `const`/`let` — never `var`
- Prefer `async`/`await` over `.then()` chains
- Minimize `console.log` — remove debug logs before shipping
- Do not hardcode styles inline — use CSS classes and Obsidian's CSS variables

## Unit tests

Vitest runs the plugin's pure logic in a Node environment: `pnpm test:unit` (or `pnpm test:watch` while working). The repository-wide `pnpm ci:validate` picks it up through the `test:unit` script.

- Put tests in `src/**/__tests__/<module>.test.ts`, next to the code they cover. Tests covering the test scaffolding itself live in `test/`; those two globs are the whole of `include` in `vitest.config.mts`.
- Import the module under test through the `~` alias, as the source does.
- `obsidian` ships type declarations with no runtime entry point, so `vitest.config.mts` aliases it to `test/obsidianStub.ts`. Add to that stub whatever a new test needs to load its module; use `vi.mock("obsidian")` in the test itself when the test needs to assert on a call.
- Obsidian's own objects are large. Build the slice the code path reads and cast it (`{ metadataCache: … } as unknown as App`) rather than constructing a whole `App` or `TFile`.
- Logic that needs a live vault, editor, or workspace is not covered here — extract the decision into a util and test that.

### Keeping the stub honest

The stub is hand-written, so it can be wrong about the API today and can fall behind when the `obsidian` dependency is bumped. Two mechanisms catch that. Each runs under exactly one command, so run `pnpm ci:validate` to get both.

`test/obsidianStub.conformance.ts` type-checks each stub member against the real declaration. It is type-only and matches none of the vitest globs, so only `pnpm check-types` enforces it. Keep it inside the `tsconfig.json` include, or the drift check disappears with no signal.

- Members with real behavior are fully conformant.
- Shells, which exist only so an importing module loads, are checked for the export name alone. When a shell gains behavior, move it to the conformant group.
- Every export must appear in one group or the other, so adding one without classifying it fails the build.

`test/obsidianStub.test.ts` pins the behavior the stub reimplements, which the type checker cannot see. It is type-checked like any other file, but only `pnpm test:unit` runs its assertions.

### Verifying the stub

Type declarations cannot tell you what a function returns for a given input, so do not guess it. Obsidian ships its implementation in `obsidian.asar`, in the resources directory of the installed app, and the current cases were settled by reading it. Two details it settled: `normalizePath("/")` returns `"/"`, and `TFolder.isRoot()` tests `path === "/"` rather than a null parent.

The bundle is minified, so it takes two steps: find the exported name to learn its minified name, then find that function. The example below is a macOS path; on Windows and Linux locate `obsidian.asar` under the install directory and substitute it.

```
node -e 'const s=require("fs").readFileSync("/Applications/Obsidian.app/Contents/Resources/obsidian.asar","utf8");
  const i=s.indexOf("normalizePath:()=>");
  console.log(s.slice(i, i+80));'
```

Read the behavior and reimplement it; do not paste the bundle's code into this repository. Pin whatever you learn in `obsidianStub.test.ts`, and name the test `diverges: …` when the stub deliberately does something else.

its own config and process because @repo/eslint-config loads
eslint-plugin-only-warn, which patches ESLint globally on import and forces
every rule to "warn". The subset the scanner keeps at error is also
registered in the app's eslint.config.mjs so editors surface it.

The real scanner additionally downgrades non-security rules to warnings.
Obsidian's published config does not replicate that, and neither do we, so
this reports a superset: stricter than the real scan, never laxer.

CI runs it through reviewdog with filter-mode=added, so existing findings
are reported without blocking while newly added ones fail.

content.text:
Pushed. Here's the answer to your question.

## The documentation

Two official sources, both found and now used:

1. **[`obsidianmd/eslint-plugin` → `docs/configuration.md`](https://github.com/obsidianmd/eslint-plugin/blob/master/docs/configuration.md)** — section *"Community Plugin Scanner Configuration"*, which states plainly:
   > "The Obsidian community plugin directory runs automated reviews using a modified version of the recommended config."
   
   It publishes the complete scanner-equivalent `eslint.config.mjs`.

2. **[`obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows`](https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows)** — the official Action, whose `src/lint.ts` generates the scanner mirror and pins `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd: 0.4.1`, the version behind your v1.7.0 panel.

## The gap that existed

Our config was `recommended` + a hand-built ignore list. The published config is `recommended` **plus a rules-override block** we didn't have at all:

| Published config | We had | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `@typescript-eslint/no-unsafe-*` × 5 → **off** | inherited at error | ~17 false errors |
| `restrict-template-expressions`, `no-base-to-string` → **off** | at error | false errors |
| `import/no-unresolved` → **off** | at error | false errors |
| `no-undef` → **off** | on | false errors |
| `validate-manifest`, `validate-license` → **off** | on | scanner handles separately |
| `commands/no-command-in-command-id`, `no-plugin-id-in-command-id` → **off** | on | would flag your existing command ids |
| Security 6 pinned at **error** | inherited | same result, not guaranteed |
| `projectService` + `extraFileExtensions: [".json"]` | `project: true` + `tsconfigRootDir` | `manifest.json` linted differently |
| `defineConfig` + `globalIgnores` | raw array | **this is why my transforms kept crashing** |
| 30-entry explicit ignore list | hand-built `flatMap` | drifted: missing `**/.obsidian/**`, `**/*.spec.ts`, `**/testUtils**` |

The `defineConfig` wrapper turned out to be the load-bearing piece. Every attempt I made to add an override block to a raw array failed with `could not find plugin "@typescript-eslint"`; under `defineConfig` the identical block just works.

## Closed

`lint:scanner` now runs Obsidian's published config **verbatim**:

| | errors | warnings |
|---|---|---|
| Before | 126 | 92 |
| Now (published config) | **114** | 78 |

The 12 that disappeared were the `no-unsafe-*` family and friends — false positives the scanner explicitly turns off. Your editor still surfaces 58 blocking-rule findings; types, lockfile, and CI all pass.

## One gap I deliberately left

The real scanner also downgrades non-security rules from error to warning. **Obsidian's own docs decline to replicate this:**

> "The actual scanner adjusts non-security rule severities from error to warning, though the configuration above maintains the recommended defaults."

So `lint:scanner` reports a superset — stricter than the real scan, never laxer. Of the 114, roughly 54 map to rules the scanner actually keeps at error. I tried three ways to reproduce the downgrade and each broke on upstream defects in `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` (a misspelled core rule `no-prototype-bultins`, still present in 0.4.2; config blocks applying rules whose plugin they don't declare). Matching Obsidian's published position is the maintainable call.

If you want exactness rather than a superset, the route is `obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows@v1` as a CI job — it implements the downgrade properly. Its docs show no working-directory input, so it'd need testing against `apps/obsidian`. Say the word and I'll try it.

content.text:
Fair challenge — and re-examining it, **my "only" was wrong.** Let me separate what's actually exact from what isn't.

## Three different things, only one is a superset

**1. The rule set — already exact.** `lint:scanner` runs Obsidian's published config verbatim: same `recommended` base, same 13 `off` overrides, same 6 security errors, same 30-entry ignore list, same `files` glob. No gap.

**2. Severity — currently a superset.** The real scanner downgrades non-security rules error→warn and keeps ~20 at error. We report all 114 as errors; only ~54 would actually block you.

**3. The real bot — not knowable.** Upstream issues [#178](https://github.com/obsidianmd/eslint-plugin/issues/178) and [#182](https://github.com/obsidianmd/eslint-plugin/issues/182) report the production scanner behaving differently from local runs, including ignoring repo-level config exemptions. No local setup fixes that.

So the gap is only #2.

## Why I said it couldn't be closed — and why that was too narrow

I tried to do the downgrade **inside the ESLint config**, three ways, and each broke:

- Rewriting `recommended`'s blocks (`{...block, rules: toWarns(block.rules)}`) → `could not find plugin "@typescript-eslint"`, because those blocks inherit plugins through `extends` chains that don't survive being recreated.
- Injecting plugins into every block → core JS rules started running on `package.json` and crashed on `sourceCode.getAllComments`.
- A trailing block downgrading every rule name → ran, but flattened the upstream file-scoping and produced 3371 warnings, and **missed rules defined inside `extends` chains**, which is why `depend/ban-dependencies` stayed at error.

All true. But I then concluded "therefore superset only," and that conflates *"config transformation is impractical"* with *"exact severity is impossible."* It isn't — **the remapping doesn't have to happen in the config.**

## How to actually close it

Run the published config through the `ESLint` class API and remap severities in the *results*, before reporting:

```js
const results = await new ESLint({ overrideConfigFile: "eslint.config.scanner.mjs" }).lintFiles(["."]);
// severity = 2 if rule is in errorRules or starts with "eslint-comments/", else 1
```

That's roughly 25 lines, and it sidesteps flat-config internals entirely. We already have `errorRules` — the authoritative list ported from `obsidian-workflows/src/lint.ts`. Result: `lint:scanner` reports ~54 errors and ~60 warnings instead of 114 errors, and exits non-zero only on the ones that actually block installability.

**Cost:** a script instead of a plain `eslint` invocation, and the error list is a hand-ported copy that could drift when the plugin bumps — which is exactly the kind of embedded copy your CLAUDE.md warns against. Mitigable by deriving it at runtime from the installed plugin rather than hardcoding, though I'd need to check whether 0.4.2 exposes it.

# Obsidian Workflows: Scanner Lint & Configuration

## Scanner Lint Rulesets

"In release mode (or when `scanner-lint: true`), the action installs and runs the
same lint configurations used by the Obsidian community directory scanner"

The specific tools deployed include:
- **Stylelint** with the scanner's ruleset (applicable to plugins and themes)
- **ESLint** with `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` (plugins only, including type-aware rules when `tsconfig.json` is present)

This ensures community directory compatibility upon submission.

## Lint Configuration

The `lint` input controls whether linting runs (default: `true`). By default, the action uses your project's own configuration. However, setting `scanner-lint: true` switches to community scanner rulesets. The documentation notes that in release mode, scanner linting is "Always forced `true`."

The content does not document specific rule severities (errors vs. warnings vs. off) beyond noting that "Policy findings are advisory by default" and reported as warnings, while "Correctness failures remain hard errors."

## Input Parameters

| Input | Default | Purpose |
|-------|---------|---------|
| `type` | `auto` | Project type: `plugin`, `theme`, or `auto` |
| `mode` | `pr` | Run mode: `pr` (CI checks) or `release` |
| `build` | _(empty)_ | Explicit build command override |
| `lint` | `true` | Enable/disable linting |
| `scanner-lint` | `false` | Use community scanner rulesets |
| `strict` | `false` | Fail on policy findings |
| `node-version` | `24` | Node.js version (minimum: 20) |

## Example Workflows

The documentation provides CI and release workflow examples but does not address monorepos or working directory configuration.

content.text:
Mirrored it, and it works better than my script — which I've deleted. CI green, `MERGEABLE`.

## What we ripped

From [`obsidian-workflows/src/lint.ts`](https://github.com/obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows/blob/main/src/lint.ts), now in `packages/eslint-config/obsidian-scanner.js`:

- **`toWarns()` verbatim** — the downgrade function. The line that mattered:
  ```js
  if (result.extends) result.extends = toWarns(result.extends);
  ```
  My versions only walked `block.rules`. Most severities live in **extended** configs, so mine silently missed them and then broke on plugin resolution. That one recursion is why theirs works and mine didn't.
- The 16 re-escalated error rules, the 4 `eslint-comments` errors, the `off`/`warn` overrides
- `linterOptions`: `noInlineConfig: false`, `reportUnusedDisableDirectives: "off"`
- The file glob `**/*.{ts,cts,mts,tsx,js,cjs,mjs,jsx}`

## How they run it

They install pinned deps into a scratch dir, write a temp `eslint.config.scanner.mjs`, then:

```js
npx --prefix <scannerDir> eslint --config <configPath> \
    --format json --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern .
```

with `cwd` = the workspace and `NODE_PATH` joining both `node_modules` trees. Plain ESLint CLI — no magic. That's exactly what our `lint:scanner` now does, minus the scratch-dir install.

## Result

| | errors | warnings |
|---|---|---|
| Published docs config (no downgrade) | 114 | 78 |
| My remapping script | 55 | 137 |
| **Now — their `toWarns` at config level** | **67** | **122** |

Config-level is the right answer and the script is gone.

**The 67 vs 55 gap is informative.** My script wrongly downgraded 12 `Definition for rule ... was not found` errors — from `eslint-disable` comments in our source naming `preferArrows/*` and `react-hooks/*`, plugins the scanner doesn't register. Those aren't rule findings whose severity can be downgraded; they're config errors. **The real scanner will hit them too**, once it can parse `.tsx`. So they're 12 additional blockers you'd otherwise have discovered at release time.

## Two fidelity gaps left

**Version skew.** The Action pins `eslint 9.37.0`, `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd 0.4.1`, `typescript-eslint 8.61.1`. We run `9.39.5` / `0.4.2` / `8.67.0` — I upgraded the plugin to 0.4.2 mid-investigation. The real scanner is most likely on 0.4.1. Pinning to match is a one-line change if you want it; leaving it means we may see rules 0.4.2 added that the scanner doesn't run yet.

**The real bot still diverges** from any local mirror ([#178](https://github.com/obsidianmd/eslint-plugin/issues/178), [#182](https://github.com/obsidianmd/eslint-plugin/issues/182)) — it ignores repo-level config exemptions and runs type-aware rules without resolved deps. **Review branch** on your directory entry remains the only ground truth.

Want me to pin to the Action's versions?

Pinned and pushed. All checks green, `MERGEABLE`.

## What's pinned

| Package | Version | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `eslint` | `9.37.0` | `apps/obsidian` only |
| `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` | `0.4.1` | both declaring packages |
| `typescript-eslint` | `8.61.1` | `packages/eslint-config` |

All exact, matching what `obsidian-workflows` installs.

## One deviation from a literal reading of your ask

I did **not** pin `eslint` in the catalog. It's shared by 8 packages, so changing it there would downgrade Roam, the website, and five packages for no benefit. Instead I replaced `catalog:` with `9.37.0` in `apps/obsidian/package.json` only, which is where the scanner actually runs. Everyone else stays on `^9.39.5`.

`typescript-eslint` had no such escape hatch — it lives only in the shared `packages/eslint-config`, so pinning it does reach Roam and the website. I A/B'd that rather than assume:

| | `8.67.0` | `8.61.1` |
|---|---|---|
| Roam | 512 problems / 0 errors | **512 / 0** |
| Website | 86 problems / 0 errors | **86 / 0** |

Byte-identical, so the shared pin is free. Had it not been, I'd have come back to you before shipping it.

## Result

`lint:scanner` still reports **67 errors / 122 warnings** — unchanged by the version pin, which is a reassuring sign that 0.4.2 hadn't introduced drift. Obsidian lint, `check-types`, and `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` all pass.

The PR is now 10 files, no source changes, and running the same rules at the same versions as the directory scanner. Your `console.log("isInside")` is still uncommitted and out of it.

Remaining known gaps, both outside our control: the production bot [ignores repo-level config exemptions](https://github.com/obsidianmd/eslint-plugin/issues/178) and [runs type-aware rules without resolved deps](https://github.com/obsidianmd/eslint-plugin/issues/182), so **Review branch** stays the ground truth — particularly given your scan currently fails at dependency install and never reaches `.tsx` files at all.

You were right to push back. I've reverted both downgrades.

## The test that settled it

Only the plugin pinned, eslint and typescript-eslint back on current versions:

| Config | Result |
|---|---|
| eslint `9.37.0` + tseslint `8.61.1` + plugin `0.4.1` | 67 errors / 122 warnings |
| eslint `9.39.5` + tseslint `8.67.0` + plugin `0.4.1` | **67 errors / 122 warnings** |

Identical. Those two downgrades changed **nothing** — I traded away your recent upgrade for zero fidelity gain.

## What's pinned now

Only `eslint-plugin-obsidianmd` at `0.4.1`, in both packages that declare it. That one earns its place: the plugin *is* the rule set, and 0.4.2 could add rules the scanner doesn't run yet, producing findings that would never appear in a real scan. eslint and typescript-eslint just execute those rules, which the measurement confirms.

`apps/obsidian` is back on `eslint: catalog:` — no version skew inside the monorepo — and `packages/eslint-config` is back on `typescript-eslint: ^8.67.0`, so Roam and the website are untouched.

## Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| `lint:scanner` | 67 errors / 122 warnings |
| `pnpm lint` (obsidian) | 144 / 0 errors |
| Roam | 512 / 0 errors |
| Website | 86 / 0 errors |
| `check-types` | pass |
| CI | all green, `MERGEABLE` |

## What I should have done

I had the context — this whole ticket exists *because* the old PR forced that upgrade — and I still executed the pin without connecting it. The right move was to check whether each pin changed anything before proposing it, and to raise the conflict with your upgrade. "Match the reference implementation" is a weak reason to move a version when the output is provably identical.

The PR is 10 files, no source changes. Your `console.log("isInside")` remains uncommitted and out of it.

## Plugin Store Guidelines

The Obsidian community directory scans every release with
`eslint-plugin-obsidianmd`, and its errors block the plugin from being
installable. Run the same rules before opening a PR:

```
pnpm --dir apps/obsidian lint:scanner
```

This is deliberately separate from `pnpm lint`. The shared repo config loads
`eslint-plugin-only-warn`, which forces every rule to "warn", so scanner
findings would be indistinguishable from style advice. `lint:scanner` runs
Obsidian's own published scanner-equivalent config in its own process. Note it
is stricter than the real scan, which additionally downgrades non-security rules
to warnings; Obsidian documents that difference.

The authoritative check is the directory itself: use **Review branch** on the
entry's management page at community.obsidian.md to scan any branch without
cutting a release. Obsidian also publishes `obsidianmd/obsidian-workflows` as a
GitHub Action that mirrors the scanner.

CI runs `lint:scanner` through reviewdog, so a finding on a line your PR adds
fails the build; pre-existing ones are reported but tolerated.

The re-escalated subset is separately registered in `apps/obsidian/eslint.config.mjs` so editors surface it, with `.vscode/settings.json` mapping `obsidianmd/*` to error for display.

**Risk / follow-up:** 67 findings exist on main and are reported without blocking, so the gate cannot be made fully blocking until they're cleared (tracked separately). content.content:
---
name: dg-engineering-writing-style
description: Draft and revise engineering emails, chat messages, requests, follow-ups, status updates, engineering tickets, PR comments, issue reports, release notes, technical documentation, and other team writing in the shared Discourse Graphs style. Use whenever a Discourse Graphs engineer asks to write, rewrite, phrase, shorten, clarify, or polish team communication or documentation, unless they request a different style.
---

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

content.content:
---
name: dg-pr-adherence-check
description: Review a PR or local diff for adherence to Discourse Graphs code standards and PR requirements, report concerns to the author, and return a Standards check checkbox. Use before handoff or requesting review, alongside scope-check.
---

# PR adherence check

Review the final change against the repository's current rules. Remain read-only unless the user authorizes fixes or PR updates. Do not post comments, request reviews, or change ticket status as part of this check.

## Resolve the evidence

1. Use the supplied PR or resolve the current branch's PR. Read its title, base and head commits, complete diff, body, checks, and review state. For local work, compare with the merge base of the intended PR base and include staged, unstaged, and relevant untracked files. Identify unavailable metadata and explicitly exclude unrelated local work.
2. Read root `AGENTS.md`, `STYLE_GUIDE.md`, `PR_GUIDELINES.md`, and `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Read nested `AGENTS.md` files applicable to every changed path. Resolve these from the target repository, not the skill's installation directory. If reviewing changes to the rules themselves, also inspect the base versions so removing a requirement cannot silently erase a finding.
3. Resolve the Linear ticket from an explicit identifier, then the PR or branch. Use the repository's `$scope-check` skill for the `Done When` boundary and its separate Scope check output. Missing ticket access or acceptance criteria blocks the scope conclusion, not independent standards checks.
4. Use command results and manual testing evidence tied to the reviewed revision. A checked box or successful unrelated CI job is not proof of all validation. Record the reviewed head and any local changes so stale evidence is identifiable.

## Evaluate adherence

- Inspect the complete diff and enough surrounding code to assess applicable TypeScript, UI, organization, comments, documentation, hygiene, and testing rules. Focus findings on introduced or modified code, not unrelated existing debt.
- Check title and branch conventions, ticket linkage, PR body requirements, size guidance, split justification, review entry points, testing evidence, Loom, and review/check status against `PR_GUIDELINES.md`.
- Distinguish mandatory rules from preferences. Words such as “prefer” and “ideally,” the 200-line target, and the five-file guideline need judgment. Above 400 changed lines, excluding tests, check for the required explanation and review guide rather than rejecting the size alone.
- Explain concerns briefly to the PR author so they can address them; formal rule citations and evidence for each finding are not required. Do not invent exceptions, team approval, testing outcomes, or video contents. If a required document is unavailable or rules conflict without a clear applicable resolution, report the gap instead of guessing.
- Respect workflow timing: missing Loom or review evidence can be reported as outstanding before requesting review while a draft is being prepared. Do not call future post-merge steps violations on an open PR.
- Keep scope expansions in Scope check. Verification is optional. Standards check only records whether the check ran.

## Return the result

Return a copy-ready section:

```markdown
## Standards check

- [x] Ran `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata.
```

The checkbox means the review ran, not that all requirements passed. If the diff cannot be resolved or the review could not run, leave it unchecked and tell the author what blocked it. Separately make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them; do not require these details in the PR body. Rerun affected checks after changes to code, rules, or PR metadata.

content.content:
# PR guidelines

This is the repository source for the DevOps PR process. Code standards live in [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md); agent instructions live in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md). Production changes, releases, and work intake remain in DevOps.

## Scope and structure

- Use one PR per Linear ticket. You may batch very minor, unrelated changes of a few lines when they are low risk.
- Scope the ticket to one specific problem. If additional problems need attention, pause that additional work and check with the team or lead before implementing it.
- Use separate PRs for unrelated refactors, feature additions, dependency updates, and lint or style fixes. Keep scope to a single package or app when possible.
- For features spanning packages, make foundational changes such as types and shared utilities first, then use separate PRs for usage and integration.

## Size and review guidance

About 200 added plus removed lines is a useful target. Up to 400 lines is acceptable when the change is scoped and self-contained. Ideally, touch fewer than five files; repetitive mechanical changes can justify more. These are review guidelines, not automatic rejection thresholds.

Test changes do not count toward the 400-line threshold.

Above 400 changed lines, explain why the PR cannot reasonably be split. Include the main review entry points and intended testing path in Reviewer brief. Keep this concise rather than adding a file-by-file summary.

## Branches and PR metadata

- Use Linear's generated branch name through Copy Branch Name.
- For Linear-backed work, use `ENG-#### Exact Linear ticket title` as the PR title. This is the repository convention in place of the alternative title formats previously listed in DevOps.
- Start with [.github/pull_request_template.md](.github/pull_request_template.md). Treat the ticket as the source of truth rather than restating it. Follow the PR body guidance in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#pull-request-bodies).

## Before requesting review

- Run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm ci:validate` from the repository root before opening a PR or declaring it ready. Resolve failures before requesting review. A draft must disclose unresolved validation blockers.
- Check applicable build and lint commands. Manually exercise changed behavior end-to-end, including relevant edge cases and alternative flows. Verification is optional; use it when checks and results help the reviewer.
- Read the complete final diff and review it against [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md), including added and modified comments. Use inline PR comments for review-specific explanations and durable code comments for constraints future changes must preserve.
- Run `$scope-check` against the ENG ticket and final diff. Paste its Scope check section into the PR body. If `Done When` is missing, leave the checkbox unchecked and state that explicitly.
- Run `$dg-pr-adherence-check` against the final diff and PR metadata. Check the Standards check box when it has run. Make any outstanding findings or unverified requirements known to the PR author so they can address them.
- Complete the Local delegated full review required by the template, using `$dg-delegated-full-review` when no other full-review workflow is available.
- Include a Loom video for every PR, including backend, refactor, and infrastructure changes. Keep it under 2–3 minutes, show before/after for bug fixes, and narrate key decisions. Put the link in Loom video.
- Assign a reviewer when ready. Do not mark a draft ready while required evidence or reviews remain incomplete.

## After merge

Delete the PR branch after a successful merge. Creating a draft does not authorize merging or deleting branches.
